items.followUp: What would happen to a moving object if friction suddenly disappeared?

rubric.why: Shows that friction is needed for grip when walking.
rubric.how: State that without friction, people could not walk because their feet would have no grip.

rubric.why: Gives another consequence of the absence of friction.
rubric.description: Explains an effect on moving objects or vehicles.
rubric.how: Mention that moving objects would not slow down, or that vehicles would be difficult to stop.

modelAnswer: Without friction between our shoes and the ground, we would not be able to walk because our feet would have no grip.
Moving objects would not slow down due to friction, and vehicles would be difficult to stop.

items.followUp: What is an Atwood machine used to investigate?

rubric.why: Identifies the parts and arrangement that define an Atwood machine.
rubric.how: Name two masses connected by a string passing over a pulley.

rubric.why: States what the arrangement is used to study.
rubric.how: Mention that it is used to study the motion or acceleration of the connected masses.

modelAnswer: An Atwood machine consists of two masses connected by a light string passing over a smooth pulley.
It is used to study the motion and acceleration of the masses.

items.followUp: State the two conditions for a body to be in complete equilibrium.

rubric.why: Gives the force condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: Defines equilibrium in terms of the resultant force.
rubric.how: State that the resultant force acting on a body is zero.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of a body in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Give an example such as a book resting on a table.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.
For example, a book resting on a table is in equilibrium.

items.followUp: Write the formula for the orbital speed of a satellite and identify the quantities it depends on.

rubric.why: Identifies the planet's mass as a factor affecting orbital speed.
rubric.how: State that orbital speed depends on the mass of the planet.

rubric.why: Identifies orbital radius as the other factor and accepts the relation expressing both dependencies.
rubric.description: Names the orbital radius or gives the orbital-speed relation.
rubric.how: State that speed depends on the orbital radius measured from the planet's centre, or give v = √(GM/r).

modelAnswer: The orbital speed of a satellite depends on the mass M of the planet and the orbital radius r, measured from the planet’s centre.
Its relation is v = √(GM/r), where G is the universal gravitational constant.

items.followUp: How does a solar cell produce electrical energy, and what is a solar panel?

rubric.why: Describes the energy conversion performed by a solar cell.
rubric.description: States the function of a solar cell.
rubric.how: Explain that a solar cell converts sunlight or light energy into electrical energy.

rubric.why: Explains how a solar panel is formed from individual cells.
rubric.how: State that a solar panel consists of a number of solar cells connected together.

modelAnswer: A solar cell converts sunlight directly into electrical energy.
A solar panel consists of a number of solar cells connected together to provide useful electrical output.
